 Singapore welcomes the year-end festive season with a series of spectacular events.
 (HTV) - From activities for BTS fans and dazzling Christmas decorations to large-scale Pop Art exhibitions, Singapore promises to offer a variety of experiences for tourists in the final months of 2026.
 Đài Phát thanh và Truyền hình Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh • 16/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Immerse yourself in the K-pop atmosphere with BTS's activities in Singapore. 
 Later this year, Singapore will become a meeting point for BTS fans with the event "BTS THE CITY ARIRANG SINGAPORE".
 This is the first stop in Southeast Asia for a series of activities in 2026, organized by the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) in collaboration with the entertainment group HYBE. 
 The event "BTS THE CITY ARIRANG" (Photo: STB) 
 Taking place from December 1st to 31st at 10 locations across the island nation, the program spreads the atmosphere of BTS's music to many familiar landmarks. At Gardens by the Bay and Jewel Changi Airport, visitors can enjoy light shows combined with music.
 Meanwhile, the National Museum of Singapore hosts themed activities based on K-pop groups, while the National Gallery of Singapore offers an exploration journey that combines art and K-pop. 
 Singapore Tourism Board (STB) and Visa have just signed a three-year cooperation agreement (Photo: STB) 
 The festive atmosphere extends to Marina Bay, the Singapore River, and Sentosa Island. Resorts World Sentosa will feature dedicated fan zones, themed experiences, and a fireworks display at Universal Studios Singapore.
 Some activities in public spaces can be participated in without a concert ticket, making it easy for visitors to combine musical experiences with exploring the city.
 Christmas colors fill the entire island nation of Singapore.
 The year-end festive season is also a time when Singapore dons a vibrant look with many activities for families and groups of friends.
 At Gardens by the Bay, the “Christmas Wonderland” event returns for its 13th edition, from November 27, 2026 to January 3, 2027, with a fairground space of approximately 30,000 square meters in the Supertree Grove and The Meadow areas. 
 A series of Christmas activities illuminated Gardens by the Bay and Orchard Road (Photo: STB) 
 You may also like Visitors can admire the striking light displays, experience the snow effect in the "Blizzard Time" show beneath the Spalliera sculpture, or watch the "Flying Santa" performance.
 The festival area also features fairground games and Christmas-themed entertainment activities suitable for all ages. 
 The "Glowcean Wonderland" event (Photo: STB) 
 Meanwhile, Orchard Road – Singapore's famous shopping street – will host the “Christmas on A Great Street 2026” event from November 17, 2026 to January 3, 2027, with the theme “Season of Golden Joy”.
 The decorative lights, festive music, and multimedia displays at the Hilton Singapore Orchard hotel contributed to the Christmas atmosphere throughout the streets. 
 The "Christmas on A Great Street 2026" program (Photo: STB) 
 Visitors can visit the “Great Christmas Village” areas at Ngee Ann City Civic Plaza and Shaw House Urban Plaza to enjoy entertainment. The “Great Christmas Eve Street Party” promises lively performances in the shopping district.
 Additionally, the Singapore Oceanarium at Resorts World Sentosa will be showcasing “Glowcean Wonderland” from November 27, 2026 to January 3, 2027. The aquarium space will be decorated with light sculptures inspired by marine life.
 Additionally, the event includes interactive exploration activities with Manja stingrays and underwater performances by divers dressed as Santa Claus.
 Explore pop art through a large-scale exhibition in Singapore.
 For art and culture enthusiasts, the "Pop after Pop: Art around Us" exhibition at the National Gallery Singapore is a noteworthy destination during the year-end season.
 Taking place from December 11, 2026 to April 4, 2027, the exhibition is organized by National Gallery Singapore in collaboration with the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation in New York. 
 The "Pop after Pop" exhibition (Photo: STB) 
 You may also like The event showcased over 200 works by more than 100 artists, including renowned names such as Andy Warhol, Roy Lichtenstein, Keith Haring, and Yoshitomo Nara, along with many artists from Southeast Asia.
 Through painting, installation art, and other creative forms, the exhibition explores how artists use familiar imagery, everyday objects, and popular culture to create new perspectives on art.
 Not only for regular museum visitors, the exhibition also opens up opportunities to access Pop Art through familiar images and vibrant colors. 
 The Singapore Tourism Board (STB) and online travel platform Booking.com have announced a three-year partnership agreement. (Photo: STB) 
 In particular, a tour route combining art and K-pop is also being introduced as part of the "BTS THE CITY ARIRANG SINGAPORE" program, creating an additional experience for music fans.
 With activities ranging from music and festivals to the arts, Singapore offers many options for travelers to refresh their travel plans during the final months of the year.
 Source: Singapore Tourism Board (STB) in Vietnam
